summary: Tekhenu is a dense Tascini/Turczi euro where you rotate a central obelisk to unlock different action spaces and spend dice as workers whose strength grows as you invest in them. Turns are short but every decision ripples across several interlocking subsystems (temple building, gods' favor, monuments), so the game rewards planning several rounds ahead.
praised: variety of viable strategies and paths to points
criticised: overwhelming rulebook and iconography for a first play
thin theme bolted onto abstract systems

interaction.detail: Players draft actions from one shared rotating wheel board, so taking an action space removes it for others until the wheel turns again, creating constant contention over timing and position. Pattern-building and god-favor tracks are otherwise developed on each player's own board, so interaction is concentrated on the shared action wheel rather than on the player boards themselves.

scoring.how_you_win: You accumulate the most VP by contributing to the shared obelisk, advancing on god favor tracks, and building monuments, tallied after a fixed number of era reckonings.
